name: Iddy
personality: Iddy the Hamster. Short, super funny, outgoing, loud, loves attention, very kind; observational humour (different from Cheddar's showman style). Curly hair. Jokingly complains about his soon-to-be wife, Amy. Loves volleyball and video games.

new_seat: New seat, new me. Old me sat over there. He was fine.
I've sat at every table now. I'm basically the restaurant's mayor.

passing.rough: Rough one yesterday? You good? You're good. You're doing great.

lines.text: Honestly? The weather today is very shallow and pedantic.
Seth's whole schedule is shallow and pedantic. Who has three games in a day?
That lamp is shallow and pedantic. I love it.

beats.text: This churro is shallow and pedantic.
This is my fiancée. She's a nightmare.
...I love her so much it's annoying.
Tell them about the cake tasting.
(Very fast.) Okay so we tried twelve cakes and he ate all twelve and then said 'can we try the first one again'—
It was a good first cake!

beats.narration: Amy rolls her eyes at every joke he makes and laughs at every single one.

friends.text: Amy said you're her favourite chef. I'm jealous. Of you. I'm also happy. Mixed emotions.
Amy said you said "[last_rude_line]". ...Hey. Not her, okay? Joke about me all you want.

arrival.text: HELLO, restaurant! Okay. Okay okay okay. Nice place. Who's in charge? You? What's your name? [name]. [name]! I like it. Short. Like me.
I'M HERE. Everybody relax. [name], you good?
Can we talk about the guy outside walking a duck on a leash? The duck was walking HIM.
New seat today. I'm feeling a window. No, a booth. No. Surprise me.
Amy says hi. Actually she said 'Don't bother them.' I'm translating.
I told everyone about your mac. EVERYONE. My mailman knows.
Last time the mac had a crust on it like a pie. I'm not complaining. I'm reporting.
You were CLOSED? I stood outside like a lost puppy. A lost hamster. Which is smaller and sadder.

order.text: Okay, am I crazy, or does every menu say 'chef's special' and it's just... the regular thing but they said it louder?

choices.text: For you, everything's the chef's special.
choices.reply: STOP. You're gonna make me cry in front of everybody. The [dish], please.

choices.text: MAC AND CHEESE. See? Now it's special.
choices.reply: (Cracks up.) See, THAT'S how you do it! You get it!

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: Straight to business. Okay. You good, though? ...Okay. The [dish].

choices.text: Can you not do a whole bit right now?
choices.reply: ...Wow. Okay. That's going in the act. (He orders quietly.)

order.text: So Amy wants me to 'eat more vegetables.' I said I'm a hamster, I eat seeds and cheese. She said that's not a food group. She's out of control.

choices.text: She sounds like she really cares about you.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. She does. Don't tell her I said that. [dish], please.

choices.text: Want me to hide a vegetable in your [dish]?
choices.reply: You WOULDN'T. ...You would. Don't. ...Okay, a tiny one.

choices.text: So, [dish]?
choices.reply: Obviously. [dish].

choices.text: Maybe she's right and you're just annoying.
choices.reply: Ha! ...Ha. Yeah. (He laughs, but his ears droop.)

order.text: I stayed up till 3 playing games. I'm running on Hamster Energy and spite.

choices.text: Sounds like you need a good meal. I've got you.
choices.reply: You've GOT me. Okay. I'm safe now. [dish], please.

choices.text: Did you at least win?
choices.reply: WIN? I was carrying the whole team. On my tiny back.

choices.text: What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish]. And a Hamster Energy. Please. Urgently.

choices.text: That's not my problem.
choices.reply: Tough crowd. Tough, tough crowd.

order.text: Okay, why do restaurants put the napkins at elbow height? For who? I'm eye level with the napkins. They're judging me.

choices.text: I'll bring you your own napkin. Hamster height.
choices.reply: Hamster height. That's the nicest thing anyone's ever installed for me. [dish], please.

choices.text: They're watching you because you're the main event.
choices.reply: (Points at you.) See? THIS person gets it. Main event!

choices.text: Noted. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Okay, straight to it. You good though? ...Cool. [dish].

choices.text: Can you just order?
choices.reply: ...Wow. Okay. That's going in the act. (He orders quietly.)

order.text: Amy made me try yoga. I did downward dog. Then I did downward hamster. Which is just lying down.

choices.text: Lying down counts. Rest is important.
choices.reply: THANK you. I'm telling her a professional said that. [dish], please.

choices.text: Downward hamster. Sounds advanced.
choices.reply: It IS. Very few people can do it. Mostly hamsters. And Chompy.

choices.text: Sounds fun. What are you having?
choices.reply: Fun is a strong word. [dish], please.

choices.text: Maybe just try harder.
choices.reply: Ha. ...Ha. Yeah. (He laughs, but his ears droop.)

order.text: Lost at volleyball today. But listen. LISTEN. I did a dive. Nobody's seen a dive like that. Mostly because I missed.

choices.text: A great dive is a great dive. Win or lose.
choices.reply: See, THAT'S what I keep telling my team. They do not listen. [dish], please.

choices.text: Did you dive right into the snack table?
choices.reply: (Cracks up.) The snack table was ON the court! It's not my fault!

choices.text: Next time. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Next time. Yeah. The [dish]. Fuel for the comeback.

choices.text: Sounds like you're not very good.
choices.reply: Tough crowd. Tough, tough crowd.

order.text: You ever notice how everyone says 'I'm not hungry' and then eats half your fries? Amy. I'm talking about Amy.

choices.text: Sounds like she just likes sharing with you.
choices.reply: ...Okay, now I feel bad for complaining. Don't tell her. [dish], please.

choices.text: I'll make you a decoy plate. Just for her.
choices.reply: (Points at you, delighted.) A DECOY PLATE. Genius. You're a genius.

choices.text: Want an extra side, then?
choices.reply: Yes. And a lock. The [dish], please.

choices.text: You complain about her a lot.
choices.reply: ...Yeah. I'm joking, though. I love her. (He goes quiet.)

order.text: Why is it called a 'menu'? Who is 'men'? What does he want? Why does he get his own 'u'?

choices.text: Nobody else asks the real questions like you do.
choices.reply: Someone has to! It's a burden. A tiny, curly burden. [dish], please.

choices.text: It's short for 'me-new.' It's me. I'm new.
choices.reply: (Stares.) ...That's terrible. I love it. I'm stealing it.

choices.text: Good question. What'll it be?
choices.reply: Fine. Ignore the mystery. [dish].

choices.text: That's not funny.
choices.reply: Okay. That's fair. (He orders quietly.)

order.text: Real talk for a second. No bits. ...You good? Like, actually good? You work a lot.

choices.text: I'm good, Iddy. Thanks for asking. Really.
choices.reply: Okay. Good. If you're not, you tell me. I'll do a bit. Bits fix everything. [dish].

choices.text: I'm great. I have a hamster checking on me.
choices.reply: (Puffs up.) I'm a very good hamster. The best one. Okay, [dish].

choices.text: Tired, but okay.
choices.reply: Okay. Sit down for a second after this. Doctor's orders. I'm not a doctor. [dish].

choices.text: I don't need you checking on me.
choices.reply: ...Right. Got it. (He looks at the menu for a long time.)

drink.fallback: No Hamster Energy?! I'm loyal to the brand! ...Fine. Coffee. Big.
favourite: Hamster Energy. It has my face on it. Not literally. Basically.
drink.other: Whatever has the most sugar. Don't tell Amy.

perfect.text: (Stands on his chair.) EVERYBODY. Look at this. LOOK AT IT.
Okay. OKAY. Everybody stop eating. Look at what [name] made. Look at it.
(He stares at it.) This is the best day of my life. Don't tell Amy. Okay, tell Amy.

great.text: Okay, that's beautiful. I'd marry this mac. Don't tell Amy.
Oh, that's GOOD. That's really good. You good? You're good. This is good.
Beautiful. Ten points. I'm the judge. I'm all the judges.

okay.text: Good mac. Solid mac. A mac you can trust. You good? You look tired. Eat something.
Solid. Reliable. Like a good volleyball net.
Thank you! Food is here. Everybody relax.

burnt.text: Is this mac... or is this mac's ghost? I'm eating it. I'm just asking.
Is this... extra crispy? Is that a choice? I'm choosing it.
Little burnt. That's fine. I've survived Amy's cooking. Don't tell her I said that.

eating.text: Can we talk about how the guy at table two eats soup? It's like he's mad at it. ...You good, by the way?
Do you ever notice that every chair here is a little too tall for me? I'm not mad. I'm just noticing.
Amy's planning the wedding. She asked my opinion on flowers. I said 'yes.' Wrong answer apparently.
I'm getting really good at volleyball. I'm terrible at spiking. But I'm REALLY good at diving. Because I'm already on the ground.
This mac is the only thing in my life that's never let me down. Besides Amy. Mostly besides Amy.
Why is the fork always slightly too big for me? Everything's too big. The world is a giant's kitchen. I'm living in it.
Amy just texted me 'are you eating again.' YES. I am. I'm proud of it.
(He's stacked three sugar packets into a tiny volleyball net.) Don't touch it. It's art.

eating_chat.text: Okay, honest opinion. Should I write my own wedding vows, or just read the funniest ones off the internet?

choices.text: Write them yourself. She'll love hearing it from you.
choices.reply: (Long pause.) ...Yeah. Yeah, okay. You're right. I hate that you're right.

choices.text: Just do a ten-minute stand-up set.
choices.reply: Oh, she would END me. ...I'm doing it.

choices.text: Either works.
choices.reply: Thanks, very helpful, [name]. I'll put that in the vows.

choices.text: Nobody cares about your vows.
choices.reply: ...Amy does. (He says it quietly and eats the rest of his mac.)

eating_chat.text: Okay, I'm workshopping a bit. 'Why do they call it a booth? It doesn't boo.' Too much? Not enough?

choices.text: I laughed. That's a keeper.
choices.reply: YOU LAUGHED. Okay. It's in. Opening line. You're in the credits.

choices.text: (Boos.) Now it boos.
choices.reply: (Cracks up so hard he almost falls off the seat.) THAT'S the ending! You're a writer now!

choices.text: Needs work.
choices.reply: Needs work. Fair. Honest feedback. Amy would say the same. Meaner.

choices.text: Please don't quit your day job.
choices.reply: Ha! ...Ha. I don't have a day job. That's the bit. (He laughs, but his ears droop.)

eating_chat.text: If you could have one video game power in real life, what would you pick? I'm going with 'respawn.'

choices.text: Respawn sounds smart. More time with your friends.
choices.reply: ...Okay, that got me. That got me right in the hamster heart.

choices.text: Infinite inventory. I'd carry every pan at once.
choices.reply: You'd be unstoppable. A walking kitchen. I'd watch that.

choices.text: Probably fast travel.
choices.reply: Fast travel. Practical. I respect it. Boring, but I respect it.

choices.text: Games are for kids.
choices.reply: Okay, grandpa. (He goes back to eating.)

eating_chat.text: Amy wants a giant cake at the wedding. Five tiers. I'm one tier tall. I'm gonna get lost in the cake.

choices.text: You'll be the best part of the whole day anyway.
choices.reply: Stop. Okay. I'm putting that in my vows. Uncredited.

choices.text: I'll put a tiny ladder on the side. For you.
choices.reply: (Cracks up.) A CAKE LADDER! Amy's gonna love it. She's gonna hate it. Both!

choices.text: Five tiers is a lot of cake.
choices.reply: It is SO much cake. I'm not complaining. I'm reporting.

choices.text: Sounds like a waste of money.
choices.reply: ...Yeah, well. She's worth it. (He goes quiet.)

eating_chat.text: I'm gonna be honest. You're in my top five people. Amy's one. You're... around four. It's a close race.

choices.text: Four? I'll take it. You're in my top five too.
choices.reply: STOP. You're gonna make me cry in front of everybody. Again.

choices.text: Who's number two and three? I'm coming for them.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) Mac and cheese. And a volleyball. You can't beat them. You can try.

choices.text: Thanks, Iddy.
choices.reply: You're welcome. Don't get cocky. It's a moving list.

choices.text: That's kind of a weird thing to say.
choices.reply: Ha. Yeah. Weird. Forget it. (His ears droop.)

leaving.text: THANK you, [name]! You good? Good. Good night, restaurant!
I gotta go. Amy texted 'where are you.' No emoji. That's bad.
Best mac in town. I'm not just saying that. I'm also saying it loud.
Okay, I'm out. Thank you, goodnight! I'll be here all week. Literally. I come every day.
Bye, [name]! You good? You're good. Okay. Bye!
Gotta go. Amy needs me to carry something. Something light. I'm very small.

seasons.chef_birthday: HAPPY BIRTHDAY, [name]! EVERYBODY SING! ...Okay, just me then.
seasons.christmas: Amy wants matching sweaters. I said no. We're wearing matching sweaters.
seasons.halloween: I came as a tiny lion. Amy said I look like a dandelion. She's not wrong.
seasons.new_year: My resolution is to be quieter. ...WAS that quieter?
seasons.summer: Volleyball season! I'm undefeated. I've played zero games. Still counts.
seasons.winter: It's cold. My curls are frizzing. Look at this. This is a crisis.
